requirements.statement: With `--json`, `shogun stats` prints one JSON document on stdout instead of the table and totals: a `runs` array with one object per run and a `totals` object, holding the same data as the table and totals.

criteria.text: `shogun stats --json` exits 0. Its stdout parses as exactly one JSON object with keys `runs` and `totals`, and contains neither the table header (`RUN`) nor the `total:` line.

Every object in `runs` has the keys id, status, mode, planner, reviewer, attempts, active_seconds, input_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cost_usd, usage and damaged. For a readable run the values match its state (e.g. attempts 2, active_seconds 150, input_tokens 100, cost_usd 0.5, usage "ok") and damaged is null. Runs are sorted by id, as in the table.

`totals` holds runs (count), by_status (status → count, damaged runs excluded), damaged (count), attempts, active_seconds, input_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cost_usd, spend_lower_bound and tokens_lower_bound. Their values equal those of the text totals for the same runs (e.g. attempts 6, active_seconds 750, both lower bounds true when a run is damaged).

requirements.statement: A damaged run's object also has every listed key: values that are not available are null (not zero), and `damaged` holds the damage reason.

criteria.text: For the damaged run, the keys mode, planner, reviewer, attempts, active_seconds, input_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cost_usd and usage are all present and JSON null. id is the run id, status is "damaged", and damaged is a non-empty string equal to the reason the table shows.

requirements.statement: Without `--json`, the output of `shogun stats` stays exactly as it is now.

criteria.text: The existing TestStatsCountsEveryRunAndFlagsMissingUsage assertions on the text output pass without being changed.
The diff of cmd/shogun/stats.go leaves every table and totals Fprintf/Fprintln format string and its arguments unchanged. The text path still runs in the same order when the flag is absent.
After `shogun stats --json`, the bytes of a run's state.json are the same as before the call.

steps.title: Implement `--json` in cmdStats
steps.objective: `shogun stats --json` prints one JSON document with runs and totals; the text output is unchanged.
actions: In cmdStats, after the --dir flag, add `asJSON := fs.Bool("json", false, "print runs and totals as one JSON document")`.

Add a type statsRunJSON with json tags id, status (string), mode, planner, reviewer, usage (*string), attempts (*int), active_seconds (*float64), input_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens (*int64), cost_usd (*float64), damaged (*string). No omitempty, so every key is always emitted and nil pointers become null.

Add a type statsTotalsJSON with runs int, by_status map[string]int, damaged int, attempts int, active_seconds float64, the five token sums int64, cost_usd float64, spend_lower_bound bool and tokens_lower_bound bool.

In the loop: for a damaged run, append {id, status "damaged", damaged: &r.damaged} when asJSON, otherwise write the existing damaged table row. For a readable run, append a row with pointers to the run's values when asJSON: raw ActiveSeconds (not minutes), planner/reviewer as recorded (no dash), usage from r.usage(), damaged nil. Otherwise write the existing Fprintf row. The totals accumulation (byStatus, partial, tot.*) runs in both cases. Create the tabwriter and header only on the text path, leaving their format strings untouched.

After the loop, if asJSON: fill statsTotalsJSON from len(runs), byStatus, damaged, tot.*. Set spend_lower_bound = damaged > 0 and tokens_lower_bound = len(partial) > 0 || damaged > 0. json.MarshalIndent {"runs": rows (non-nil slice), "totals": totals} with "" and " ", Fprintln it to a.stdout, return ExitOK. The existing tw.Flush and totals printing follow unchanged for the text path.
Leave the no-runs branch (stderr message, exit 0) as it is (see Q-002).

verification.expected: git diff cmd/shogun/stats.go leaves every existing table/totals format string and its arguments byte-identical. The JSON path only adds code (R-003.C2).
gofmt -l cmd/shogun prints nothing, and go vet ./cmd/shogun passes.

risks.risk: Moving the tabwriter creation behind the flag changes the text output by accident.
risks.mitigation: Keep the header and row format strings unchanged. The unchanged existing test (S-002) guards the text output.

steps.rollback_or_why_not_applicable: git checkout cmd/shogun/stats.go reverts the change; no data or state is touched.

steps.title: Test the JSON output
steps.objective: Cover the JSON document, the damaged-run nulls and read-only behaviour; keep the text test unchanged.
actions: At the end of TestStatsCountsEveryRunAndFlagsMissingUsage, leave the existing assertions as they are. Add a call to runCLI(t, ws, "stats", "--json") on the same fixtures and assert exit ExitOK.
Assert that stdout contains no "RUN" header or "total:" line. json.Unmarshal it into a map[string]any (fail if that errors) and check that it has `runs` (5 entries, sorted by id) and `totals`.

For run 20260927-000001-a, check that every listed key is present: attempts 2, active_seconds 150, input_tokens 100, cache_read_tokens 1000, output_tokens 50, reasoning_tokens 20, cost_usd 0.5, usage "ok", planner "claude/opus:high", mode "fast", damaged nil. For 20260927-000002-b, check usage "unknown".

For the damaged run 20260927-000003-c, check that each of mode, planner, reviewer, attempts, active_seconds, the five token keys, cost_usd and usage is present (comma-ok lookup) and nil. Check status "damaged" and that damaged is a non-empty string.

Check totals: runs 5, by_status {approved 1, failed 1, needs_input 1, paused 1}, damaged 1, attempts 6, active_seconds 750, input_tokens 100, cache_read_tokens 1000, cache_write_tokens 0, output_tokens 50, reasoning_tokens 20, cost_usd 0.5, spend_lower_bound true, tokens_lower_bound true.
After the --json call, compare state.json of 20260927-000001-a with `before` again.

verification.expected: go test ./cmd/shogun -run TestStats passes, including the JSON document shape and values (R-001.C1, R-001.C2, R-001.C3).
The same test's damaged-run assertions pass: all listed keys are present and null, status "damaged", damaged is the reason (R-002.C1).
git diff cmd/shogun/stats_test.go only adds lines after the existing assertions; the text assertions are unchanged and pass (R-003.C1).

steps.rollback_or_why_not_applicable: git checkout cmd/shogun/stats_test.go reverts the test addition.

questions.question: For a damaged run, should `status` be the string "damaged" (as in the table's STATUS column) or null?
questions.why: The task says unavailable values are null and `damaged` holds the reason, but the table shows "damaged" as the status. The planned test fixes one of the two.
questions.impact: The value of `status` for damaged runs, and the assertion in S-002.
options: status = null (the real status cannot be read)
questions.proposed_assumption: status = "damaged", mirroring the table. This is a one-line change if null is wanted.

questions.question: With `--json` and no runs in the directory, should stats keep today's behaviour (message on stderr, empty stdout, exit 0) or print a JSON document with empty `runs` and zero totals?
questions.why: The task does not cover the empty case. A JSON consumer may expect a document every time.
questions.impact: Only the no-runs branch of cmdStats.
options: Keep the current stderr message and empty stdout
questions.proposed_assumption: Keep the current behaviour unchanged (smallest change). This is easy to change later.
